title: Auto layout that behaves
goal: You will build a profile card whose text and button resize predictably using nested auto layout frames.
prerequisites: The Layers and Design panels visible

steps.action: Draw a frame about 360 pixels wide and 240 pixels tall on the canvas.
steps.where: Frame tool in the top toolbar, or the F keyboard shortcut.
steps.why: This frame will become the responsive profile card.
steps.checkpoint: A new frame appears on the canvas and in the Layers panel.
hint_levels: Look for the frame-shaped tool in the top toolbar.
Select Frame, then drag an empty rectangular area on the canvas.
Press F, then drag on the canvas until the width and height fields in the right Design panel are near 360 and 240.

steps.action: Add the text "Jordan Lee" inside the frame.
steps.where: Text tool in the top toolbar, or the T keyboard shortcut.
steps.why: The name provides the card's primary content layer.
steps.checkpoint: The text "Jordan Lee" is visible inside the frame and nested beneath it in the Layers panel.
hint_levels: Use the tool marked with a T.
Click once inside the frame before typing the name.
Press T, click near the frame's upper-left corner, type Jordan Lee, then press Esc.

steps.action: Add the text "Product Designer" below the name.
steps.where: Text tool in the top toolbar, or the T keyboard shortcut.
steps.why: A second layer makes spacing and vertical direction visible.
steps.checkpoint: The role text appears below the name as a separate layer in the Layers panel.
hint_levels: Create another text layer beneath the first one.
Activate the Text tool again and click below Jordan Lee.
Press T, click below the name, type Product Designer, then press Esc.

steps.action: Apply auto layout to the card frame and set its direction to vertical.
steps.where: Auto layout section of the right Design panel after selecting the outer frame.
steps.why: Vertical auto layout keeps the card's children arranged from top to bottom.
steps.checkpoint: The name and role form a vertical stack, and the Auto layout section shows the vertical direction icon selected.
hint_levels: Select the outer frame and look for Auto layout on the right.
Add auto layout, then choose the arrow that points downward.
Click the outer frame in the Layers panel, press Shift+A, then click the Vertical direction icon in Design > Auto layout.

steps.action: Set the card's gap to 16 and its padding on all sides to 24.
steps.where: Gap between items and padding fields in the right Design panel's Auto layout section.
steps.why: Gap controls space between children while padding controls space around the card's inside edges.
steps.checkpoint: The two text layers are 16 pixels apart and sit 24 pixels from the frame edges.
hint_levels: Find the numeric spacing controls beside the auto layout diagram.
Set Gap between items separately from the padding values.
Select the card, enter 16 in Gap between items, then enter 24 in the horizontal and vertical padding fields under Design > Auto layout.

steps.action: Turn the two text layers into a nested vertical auto layout frame.
steps.where: Layers panel and the Auto layout button in the right Design panel, or Shift+A.
steps.why: A nested frame lets the text group manage its own spacing independently of the card.
steps.checkpoint: A new frame containing both text layers appears inside the card in the Layers panel.
hint_levels: Select both text layers before adding auto layout.
Use Shift-click in Layers to select Jordan Lee and Product Designer together.
In the Layers panel click Jordan Lee, Shift-click Product Designer, press Shift+A, then select the Vertical direction icon in Design > Auto layout.

steps.action: Set the nested text frame to Fill container width and Hug contents height.
steps.where: Width and height resizing controls near the top of the right Design panel.
steps.why: Fill makes the text group follow the card's width while Hug keeps its height fitted to its content.
steps.checkpoint: The nested frame spans the card's available width without adding empty vertical space.
hint_levels: Select the new inner frame and inspect its width and height modes.
Choose Fill container for width and Hug contents for height.
Select the nested text frame in Layers, open the width dropdown in the right Design panel and choose Fill container, then open the height dropdown and choose Hug contents.

steps.action: Add the text "View profile" as a new child at the bottom of the card.
steps.where: Text tool in the top toolbar and the outer card frame on the canvas.
steps.why: This text will become a nested auto layout button.
steps.checkpoint: "View profile" appears below the text group and as another child of the outer card in the Layers panel.
hint_levels: Place a new text layer after the nested text frame.
Make sure the text lands inside the outer card rather than outside it.
Press T, click near the bottom inside the card, type View profile, then press Esc; drag its layer beneath the nested text frame in Layers if needed.

steps.action: Wrap "View profile" in auto layout and give its new frame 12 pixels vertical padding and 16 pixels horizontal padding.
steps.where: Auto layout and padding controls in the right Design panel after selecting the button text.
steps.why: Hug sizing plus padding creates a button that grows with its label.
steps.checkpoint: A frame surrounds the label with visible space above, below, left, and right, and both resizing modes show Hug contents.
hint_levels: Turn the label itself into an auto layout frame.
Select View profile, add auto layout, and edit the new frame's padding.
Click View profile in Layers, press Shift+A, then enter 12 for vertical padding and 16 for horizontal padding in Design > Auto layout; leave width and height on Hug contents.

steps.action: Change the button frame's width from Hug contents to Fill container.
steps.where: Width resizing dropdown near the top of the right Design panel.
steps.why: The button will now expand and contract with the available card width.
steps.checkpoint: The button frame stretches across the card while its label remains inside the padded area.
hint_levels: Select the button's frame rather than its text.
The width mode should follow the parent instead of the label.
Click the button frame in Layers, open the width dropdown in the right Design panel, and choose Fill container.

steps.action: Set the outer card frame's height to Hug contents.
steps.where: Height resizing dropdown near the top of the right Design panel.
steps.why: The card's height will follow its nested content, gaps, and padding automatically.
steps.checkpoint: The card's bottom edge fits 24 pixels below the button instead of retaining unused height.
hint_levels: Select the outermost frame and inspect its height mode.
Replace the fixed height with a content-driven height.
Click the outer card frame in Layers, open the height dropdown in the right Design panel, and choose Hug contents.

steps.action: Drag the outer card's right edge wider and then narrower.
steps.where: Right resize handle on the selected outer frame on the canvas.
steps.why: This tests whether Fill and Hug resizing behaviors work through the nested frames.
steps.checkpoint: The text group and button follow the card's width while the card's height and internal padding remain stable.
hint_levels: Resize only the outer frame and watch its children.
Use the middle handle on the card's right edge so only its width changes.
Select the outer card, drag the middle-right handle horizontally, and confirm the Fill container children resize without changing the 16-pixel gap or 24-pixel card padding.
